## 1. One-paragraph verdict
A genuine machine-written HLS playlist: generated by ffmpeg 7.1.5 itself
(`-f segment -segment_time 2.5 -segment_list pl.m3u8 -segment_list_type m3u8`,
hls_vod_e2e.rs:9-16) for the raw-AAC lane of the HLS VOD e2e suite. Structure
verified: VERSION 3, MEDIA-SEQUENCE 0, ALLOW-CACHE YES, TARGETDURATION 3 (=
round of max EXTINF 2.507755 — spec-correct), 4 EXTINF segments in playlist
order (seg000-3.aac, durations 2.507755/2.507755/2.484535/0.523175, sum 8.023 s
≈ the 8 s sine), ENDLIST. Consumed by a green baseline test that proves the
whole stack on top of it.

## 2. What actually works (verified)
— python3: 227 B, sha256 above; EXTINF sum 8.023220 s; segment names match the
dir contents (seg000-003.aac all present) and the consumer's SEGMENTS const
(hls_vod_e2e.rs:53).
— Consumer green: baseline cargo-test-workspace.txt:5674
`adts_lane_is_byte_exact_and_decodes_to_the_ffmpeg_oracle ... ok`
(hls_vod_e2e.rs:255-320): serves the lane over a real socket (MockServer),
opens `hls/adts_vod/pl.m3u8` through the VOD session (:257), asserts the
streamed bytes == on-disk cat(segments), demuxes a second session through
AdtsDemuxer (codec `aac-lc`), and decodes to the ffmpeg oracle
(ORACLE_AAC_PACKETS=346, :49/:53). The wire-shape assertion (:317) proves the
playlist is parsed (playlist fetched first, then segments in playlist order).
The ts-lane sibling over the same fixture family is green too (:5673).
— Provenance: ffmpeg-generated per the module header (:9-16); documented in
docs/worklog/archive-2026-10.md:10794 and the compat-matrix corpus
(docs/corpus/compat-matrix-20261110.raw-rows.jsonl:84-87 decode the segments
with pcm_md5 per segment — the lane has executed decode evidence).

## 3. Findings
None. Checked: playlist syntax vs HLS spec (TARGETDURATION rounding rule —
correct), segment-name/dir/consumer agreement (3-way match), duration-sum vs
the documented 8 s content (8.023 s — honest prose rounding, 0.3%), ENDLIST/VOD
shape vs the VOD-session consumer, duplicate-vs-playlists-crate (no copy — the
playlists crate's ts_vod playlist is a DIFFERENT file), execution evidence
(baseline green + per-segment pcm_md5 matrix rows).

## 4. Matrix evidence
The lane's compat-matrix rows are per-SEGMENT (raw-rows.jsonl:84-87: seg000-2
decoded, aac-lc, 108/108/107 packets, pcm_md5s recorded); the playlist itself
is the lane's wiring artifact, cited by the e2e test and the corpus doc — no
row pins the playlist bytes directly (no sha pin anywhere; behavioral pins are
the byte-parity + oracle constants — stronger than a sha pin here).

## 5. Open questions for the next agent
- If a lane-level sha pin is ever wanted, follow the mp4_mjpeg_pcm.oracle.sha256
  sidecar pattern; today drift would surface as e2e failure only if it changed
  segment order/count — a duration-only edit would pass silently (acceptable:
  durations are informational in the VOD byte-parity lane).
